customers.name: Portfolio and Trading Manager
customers.description: Sources and hedges the electricity and gas portfolio of a supplier or trading company, maintains the price curves and the cost-plus pricing that every proposition and B2B quote is built on, and watches positions, volumes, value and risk per customer segment. Typical employer: the portfolio desk of a Dutch supplier such as Pure Energie, Vattenfall or PZEM, or the Benelux origination and portfolio team of an international BRP such as Axpo or TotalEnergies, running a portfolio of a few hundred GWh to several TWh a year with a desk of three to ten traders and analysts. Since the day-ahead market moved to 15-minute blocks on 30 September 2025 the desk values its position 96 times a day instead of 24, and every retail proposition, every producer PPA and every industrial click contract changes that position.
careAbout: A hedging strategy that is executed as planned: forward, day-ahead and PPA volumes covering the forecast demand of each segment within the agreed open-position limits, with the coverage visible per delivery period

One price curve set — forward curves, EPEX 15-minute day-ahead, TTF gas, guarantees of origin, imbalance and profile costs — that feeds cost-plus pricing so that retail tariffs, B2B quotes and click contracts are priced from the same numbers the portfolio is valued on

Positions, volumes and value per segment (residential fixed, variable, dynamic, B2B multi-site, producers, flex assets) updated every 15 minutes from allocation and forecast data rather than from a weekly spreadsheet
Risk exposures (volume risk from churn and weather, price risk on open positions, profile and imbalance cost) spotted before they hit the margin, with an action attached to every deviation
B2B deals priced from the actual portfolio position and profile cost, with a quote out in hours and the margin tracked after the deal closes
A sourcing cost and gross margin per MWh the CFO can reconcile to the settlement invoices and the billing runs
winsThem: Position tracking that combines allocated volumes from Allocation 2.0, portfolio forecasts and executed hedges per segment and per 15-minute block, so the open position is a number on a screen and not the result of a Monday-morning export
Price curves and cost-plus pricing maintained once and pushed to the proposition builder, the quoting tool and the customer trading desk, ending the drift between what was priced and what was sourced
Hedge transactions captured where they are executed and immediately reflected in coverage, value and risk, with limits that alert instead of being checked at month end
A 15-minute financial view per segment that shows where margin is made or lost, which the desk can share with the CFO and the proposition team without a translation layer
Deal structuring for B2B contracts (fixed, tranche, click, pass-through) that produces the quote, the risk reservation and the contract terms from the same profile and curve data
theirFear: A retail campaign that sells thousands of fixed contracts while the desk is under-hedged, so the portfolio buys the volume at a market price far above the tariff and the campaign becomes the year's biggest loss
A price curve updated in the pricing tool but not in the position valuation, so the desk reports a margin that the settlement invoice later contradicts
An industrial click contract executed by a customer at a price the desk had not hedged, discovered only when the position report shows an open volume for the whole delivery year

jobsToBeDone.name: Source and hedge the portfolio at the right cost and risk
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: From the demand and production forecast per segment to a portfolio that is procured on forward, day-ahead and PPA markets according to a hedging strategy, with open positions kept inside risk limits and the sourcing cost reported against the margin the propositions were priced on.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: The portfolio is covered as the strategy prescribes for every delivery period, hedges are executed with little slippage, open positions stay within limits as customers come and go, and the sourcing cost per MWh is known and reconcilable at all times.

steps.step: Build the demand and production forecast per segment
steps.description: Combine contract volumes, allocated history, weather-driven profiles, solar and wind production and expected churn and inflow into a volume forecast per segment and delivery period, from tomorrow's 15-minute blocks to the forward years the desk hedges.

streamsNeeded.name: Forecast and Nominate the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Produces the day-ahead, intraday and long-horizon portfolio forecast per segment that the hedging plan is built on.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect and Validate Meter Data
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Supplies validated consumption and production history per connection so segment profiles reflect what was really used.

steps.step: Define the hedging strategy and open-position limits
steps.description: Decide per segment how much of the forecast volume is hedged how far ahead (for example a fixed-price residential book hedged in tranches over two years, a dynamic book left to day-ahead), set open-position and value-at-risk limits, and record who may deviate from them.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Holds the hedging strategy, tranche schedules and risk limits per segment as the reference the desk executes and is measured against.

steps.step: Execute hedges on forward, day-ahead and PPA markets
steps.description: Buy or sell forward products, place day-ahead orders for the residual volume, and contract PPAs with wind and solar producers; capture every transaction with its delivery profile, counterparty and price so it lands in the position immediately.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Captures hedge transactions and PPAs and applies them to coverage and value per delivery period.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Connects broker, exchange and price-data feeds so executed trades and market prices arrive without re-keying.

steps.step: Track hedge coverage and rebalance as the portfolio changes
steps.description: Watch the coverage ratio per segment and period as switches, move-ins, churn, new campaigns and producer connections change the forecast volume; rebalance by buying or selling the difference before the open position exceeds its limit.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Recalculates coverage and the open position whenever the forecast or the hedge book changes and alerts on limit breaches.

streamsNeeded.name: Onboard and Switch Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Feeds confirmed switches, move-ins and terminations into the volume forecast so the desk sees inflow and churn as they happen.

steps.step: Report sourcing cost and risk to management
steps.description: Produce the weekly and monthly view of sourcing cost per MWh, coverage, open positions, realised versus priced margin and risk exposures per segment, reconciled to settlement invoices and billing, for the CFO and the risk committee.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Aggregates sourcing cost, margin and risk per segment into the reporting the risk committee reviews.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the settled volumes and imbalance costs that the reported sourcing cost is reconciled against.

jobsToBeDone.name: See positions, volumes and value per segment every 15 minutes
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Keep a live view of the portfolio per customer segment and per 15-minute block: allocated and forecast volumes, hedged volumes, valuation against current price curves, and the risks and deviations that need an action, so the desk steers the portfolio on facts instead of month-old reports.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: The desk, the proposition team and the CFO look at the same position, volume and value per segment, refreshed every 15 minutes, and every deviation from plan has an owner and an action before it becomes a settlement surprise.

steps.step: Define segments and attribute every contract to one
steps.description: Set up the segments the portfolio is steered on (residential fixed, variable, dynamic, EV and battery propositions, B2B multi-site, producers, flex assets) and the rules that attribute each supply contract, PPA and connection to a segment as propositions are launched or changed.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Maintains the segment structure and the attribution rules that all positions and values are grouped by.

streamsNeeded.name: Launch Energy Propositions and Tariffs
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Tags every new proposition with its segment and pricing basis at launch so contracts land in the right position from the first sale.

steps.step: Get allocated and forecast volumes per segment per 15-minute block
steps.description: Pull the allocated volumes from Allocation 2.0, the validated telemetry of large connections and the portfolio forecast for periods not yet allocated, and aggregate them per segment and 15-minute block for the current day, the week and the delivery months ahead.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Delivers the allocated volumes per connection type and interval that make up the realised part of the position.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect and Validate Meter Data
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides near real-time telemetry of large and flexible connections for the intervals allocation has not yet covered.

streamsNeeded.name: Forecast and Nominate the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Fills the forward part of the position with the forecast per segment used for nominations.

steps.step: Value positions against the current price curves
steps.description: Value the hedged and open volumes per segment against the forward curves, the 15-minute day-ahead prices and the TTF gas curve, including profile, imbalance and guarantee-of-origin costs, so margin per segment is a number that updates with the market.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Applies the maintained price curves and cost components to positions to produce value and margin per segment.

steps.step: Spot risks and deviations that need an action
steps.description: Compare the position against the hedging plan and the risk limits, and detect the deviations that matter: a segment growing faster than hedged, a producer PPA under-delivering, an intraday position drifting, a curve move that turns a segment's margin negative.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs the limit and deviation checks and raises alerts with the segment, period and size of the exposure.

streamsNeeded.name: Steer Intraday and Optimise Imbalance
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Shows the intraday position and the expected imbalance so short-term deviations are visible next to the long-term ones.

steps.step: Take action: rebalance, re-price or steer
steps.description: Turn each deviation into an action: an additional hedge, a tariff or price-curve update for the proposition team, a request to the BRP desk to steer intraday, or a hold on a campaign, and record the decision against the position it addressed.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Records the rebalancing trades and price-curve changes and shows their effect on coverage and margin.

streamsNeeded.name: Steer Intraday and Optimise Imbalance
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Hands the short-term part of the action to the intraday steering cycle so ETPA trades or flex steering close the gap.

jobsToBeDone.name: Price and structure B2B deals from the portfolio position
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Turn a tender or request from a business customer, a multi-site industrial or a producer into a priced and structured deal (fixed, tranche, click, pass-through or PPA) built from the customer's consumption profile, the current price curves, the profile and imbalance cost the portfolio will carry and the margin policy, and keep the deal's margin under control after signing.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Every B2B quote goes out in hours from the same curves and profile costs the portfolio is valued on, the contract structure matches what the desk can hedge, and the realised margin of the deal is tracked from the first click to the last invoice.

steps.step: Receive the request with the consumption profile
steps.description: Capture the tender or request with its sites, connection types, contract period, expected volumes and the historical consumption or production profile per site, from the sales team, the customer trading desk or a broker.

streamsNeeded.name: Trade and Manage Customer Energy Contracts
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Registers the B2B request with its sites and framework terms and routes it to pricing.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect and Validate Meter Data
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Supplies the validated interval history of the customer's connections that the profile cost is calculated from.

steps.step: Build the cost-plus price
steps.description: Calculate the price from the forward curve for the period, the profile cost of the customer's shape, the expected imbalance cost, guarantees of origin, grid and levy pass-throughs and the margin policy for the segment, with the assumptions stored on the quote.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the curves, profile and imbalance cost components and the cost-plus model that produce the price and its audit trail.

steps.step: Structure the contract
steps.description: Choose the structure that fits the customer and the portfolio: full fixed, tranches, click contract with click windows and limits, day-ahead pass-through, or a PPA for a producer; define the click rules, volume tolerance bands and the risk reservation the desk makes for it.

streamsNeeded.name: Trade and Manage Customer Energy Contracts
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Models the contract structure, click rules and tolerance bands that the customer will later trade within.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Reserves the risk and coverage for the structured volume so the deal is hedgeable before it is signed.

steps.step: Hand the deal to quoting, contracting and onboarding
steps.description: Release the priced structure to the supplier's quoting and contract process, so the offer, the multi-site supply contract and the switch of every connection are produced from the deal data without re-entry.

streamsNeeded.name: Launch Energy Propositions and Tariffs
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Turns the priced structure into a quotable B2B product with its tariff components and terms.

streamsNeeded.name: Onboard and Switch Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Creates the multi-site contract and runs the switch of each connection through market communication once the deal is signed.

steps.step: Manage clicks and track the deal's margin
steps.description: Hedge the clicks the customer executes, watch the volume against the tolerance bands, re-price on contract changes such as added sites, and compare the realised margin per deal with what was priced.

streamsNeeded.name: Trade and Manage Customer Energy Contracts
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Executes and records the customer's clicks and contract changes so the desk sees them as they happen.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Applies each click to the hedge book and reports realised versus priced margin per deal.

customerJourneyStories.name: Moving the portfolio desk off spreadsheets after the 15-minute day-ahead change
customerJourneyStories.summary: The portfolio manager of a mid-sized Dutch supplier with a growing dynamic-tariff and producer book adopts the Trade and Portfolio Suite when the 15-minute day-ahead market and Allocation 2.0 make the desk's spreadsheet positions unworkable, and ends up with a 15-minute view per segment that the CFO trusts.

stages.narrative: On 30 September 2025 the day-ahead market moves to 15-minute blocks and the desk's Excel position model, built on hourly prices and monthly allocation exports, breaks down: valuation takes a morning, the dynamic-tariff segment cannot be separated from the fixed book, and a winter campaign sold more fixed contracts than the desk had hedged. The CFO asks how much the portfolio is really worth today and gets three different answers.

The portfolio manager reads Eneve's review of the 2025 Dutch market changes, hears from the supplier's billing team that their Supplier Suite vendor also offers sourcing and pricing modules, and meets a peer desk at a TenneT market-party session that runs positions per segment on the same platform. A demo shows allocated and forecast volumes per 15-minute block, hedges applied to coverage, and value per segment on one screen.

The desk compares extending the spreadsheet model, buying a generic energy trading and risk management system, and adopting the Trade and Portfolio Suite on the platform that already holds the contracts and allocation data. Decisive checks are the segment attribution of existing contracts, how PPAs and click contracts are represented, whether the price curves can feed the proposition builder, the audit trail the risk committee needs, and the per-portfolio subscription against the analyst hours it replaces.

For one quarter the desk runs the suite in parallel: segments are defined, the hedge book is loaded, and the daily position is compared with the spreadsheet. The differences turn out to be real: two PPAs valued on the wrong profile and a segment of dynamic contracts that had been counted as fixed. The CFO signs off when the settlement invoice reconciles to the suite's numbers within one percent.

The spreadsheet is retired. The desk starts the day with the 15-minute position per segment, the hedging strategy and limits live in the suite, alerts replace the Monday export, and the proposition team prices the spring campaign from the curves the desk maintains, with the coverage check built into the launch.

At renewal the desk adds the risk analytics module and the customer trading desk for its B2B book, the CFO uses the segment margin view in the monthly close, and the portfolio manager presents the desk's setup at a supplier peer meeting. Leaving would mean rebuilding the segment history and the link to billing and allocation that now make the position trustworthy.

customerJourneyStories.name: Adopting cost-plus pricing and deal structuring for the B2B book
customerJourneyStories.summary: A portfolio and origination manager at the Benelux desk of an international BRP already running positions on the platform adopts the cost-plus pricing and deal structuring capabilities after a badly priced industrial click contract, and turns B2B quoting into a same-day process with tracked margin.

stages.narrative: An industrial customer clicks a full delivery year at a price the desk had quoted from a stale curve; the hedge is executed at a loss and the deal's margin is negative before the first delivery. The head of origination wants every quote built from the live curves and every click to hit the hedge book the same hour.

During the quarterly account review the platform's customer success manager shows the pricing and customer trading modules the desk licenses but has not switched on: cost-plus pricing from the maintained curves, contract structuring with click rules and tolerance bands, and the customer trading desk that records clicks against the position. A supplier reference describes pricing multi-site tenders in an afternoon.

The desk and the risk manager check whether the cost-plus model covers profile, imbalance and guarantee-of-origin components the way their internal policy prescribes, how click limits and windows are enforced, whether the audit trail of a quote would satisfy the trade-surveillance review, and what integration with the group's trading system is needed. Two recent tenders are re-priced in the tool and compared with the original quotes.

For two months all new B2B tenders are priced through the cost-plus model and one industrial framework contract is migrated to the customer trading desk. Quotes go out the same day, the industrial customer's clicks appear in the hedge book within the hour, and the risk manager sees the reserved volume per structured deal for the first time.

The pricing policy per segment is maintained in the suite, sales and the desk share the quote pipeline, and realised margin per deal is reviewed monthly against what was priced. Producers' PPAs are structured with the same tool and their output feeds the position directly.

The desk expands the licence to the group's Belgian portfolio when the platform's Belgian market adapters arrive, and asks for a pricing API so brokers can request indicative quotes directly. The margin discipline the tool created has become part of how the desk is measured.

top.name: Portfolio gross margin per MWh
top.description: Realised gross margin of the supply and trading portfolio per MWh delivered: contract revenue minus sourcing, profile, imbalance and guarantee-of-origin cost, per segment and in total. Modeled seed value for a mid-sized Dutch supplier portfolio, not an official Eneve or customer figure.

branches.name: Sourcing cost and hedge quality
branches.description: How well the portfolio is covered according to the hedging strategy and how close the realised sourcing cost is to the market benchmark and the priced cost.

children.name: Hedge coverage ratio
children.description: Hedged volume as a share of the forecast volume per segment and delivery period, weighted over the hedging horizon the strategy prescribes.

children.name: Open position within risk limits
children.description: Share of trading days on which the open position of every segment stayed inside its volume and value-at-risk limits.

children.name: Hedge execution slippage
children.description: Difference between the price at which a hedge was decided and the price at which it was executed, per MWh hedged.

children.name: Sourcing cost versus benchmark
children.description: Realised sourcing cost per MWh compared with the benchmark curve for the same delivery periods and profiles, positive when the desk paid more than the benchmark.

children.name: Profile cost per MWh
children.description: Cost of shaping baseload hedges to the actual consumption and production profile of the segment, per MWh delivered.

children.name: PPA and long-term contract share of volume
children.description: Share of the portfolio volume covered by power purchase agreements and long-term contracts rather than short-term market purchases.

branches.name: Position visibility and pricing discipline
branches.description: Whether the desk sees its position accurately and quickly enough to act, and whether propositions and B2B deals are priced from the same numbers the portfolio is valued on.

children.name: Forecast accuracy
children.description: One minus the mean absolute percentage error of the portfolio volume forecast per segment, measured against allocated volumes over the delivery month.

children.name: Segment volume forecast error
children.description: Mean absolute percentage error of the monthly volume forecast for the worst-performing segment, typically dynamic tariffs or producers.

children.name: Position refresh latency
children.description: Minutes between the arrival of new allocation, telemetry or hedge data and the updated position and value being visible per segment.

children.name: B2B deal margin realisation
children.description: Realised gross margin of B2B and producer deals as a share of the margin priced at quote time, over the deals in delivery.

children.name: Quote turnaround time
children.description: Working hours between receiving a B2B request with its profile and sending the priced offer.

children.name: Deals priced with the cost-plus model
children.description: Share of B2B quotes produced from the maintained price curves and cost components with a stored assumption trail, rather than priced by hand.

top.name: Portfolio volume managed on the platform
top.description: Annual electricity and gas volume of the portfolios whose sourcing, pricing and position management runs on the Trade and Portfolio Suite. Modeled seed value for the portfolio-operator segment, not an official Eneve figure.

branches.name: Trade and Portfolio Suite adoption
branches.description: How many portfolio desks run on the suite, how fast they get to a live position and how many of the sourcing, pricing, risk and customer trading modules they use.

children.name: Portfolio desks on the platform
children.description: Number of supplier and trading-company portfolio desks with an active Trade and Portfolio Suite subscription, including migrated Jules and EBASE heritage customers.

children.name: Heritage trading customers migrated
children.description: Share of Jules customer-trading and EBASE portfolio customers whose desks run on the unified platform rather than the heritage product.

children.name: Time to first live position view
children.description: Weeks from contract signature until a new desk sees its segments, hedge book and position valued on the platform.

children.name: Modules used per desk
children.description: Average number of Trade and Portfolio Suite modules (sourcing, price curves, risk analytics, customer trading, consumption self-service) active per desk.

children.name: Risk analytics attach rate
children.description: Share of portfolio desks that use the position and risk analytics module with limits and alerts.

children.name: Customer trading attach rate
children.description: Share of portfolio desks that run their B2B click contracts and customer trades through the customer trading desk.

branches.name: Portfolio segment revenue and retention
branches.description: What the portfolio-operator segment is worth in recurring revenue and how well desks are retained and expanded.

children.name: Trade and Portfolio Suite recurring revenue
children.description: Annual recurring subscription revenue from portfolio desks, scaling with portfolio volume and active modules.

children.name: Revenue per TWh managed
children.description: Annual subscription revenue divided by the portfolio volume managed on the suite.

children.name: Price and market data feed revenue
children.description: Annual revenue from price-curve, market-data and pricing API add-ons sold to portfolio desks.

children.name: Portfolio desk churn rate
children.description: Share of portfolio desks that leave the suite per year, including desks lost to in-house trading systems after an acquisition.

children.name: Net revenue retention per desk
children.description: Recurring revenue from desks that were customers a year ago, including expansion and contraction, as a share of their revenue a year ago.

children.name: Reference desks among international BRPs
children.description: Number of international BRPs and traders, such as Axpo and TotalEnergies, that act as public references for the suite.

year1.focus: Bring the Jules and EBASE portfolio and trading customers onto the unified suite, make positions per segment per 15-minute block the standard view for every desk after the 15-minute day-ahead change, and connect the maintained price curves to the proposition builder and B2B quoting.
year1.productTheme: One position, one price curve set, per 15 minutes

businessKPI.northStar: Portfolio volume managed on the platform

customers.name: BRP and Balancing Operator
customers.description: Runs the daily balance-responsibility cycle for an electricity and gas portfolio: day-ahead, intraday and ex-post forecasting per EAN type, E-programme nominations and re-nominations to TenneT and gas nominations to the gas TSO, intraday steering through the ETPA trading cycle and flexible assets, and the allocation, reconciliation, imbalance settlement and BRP compliance reporting that follow under Allocation 2.0. Typical employer: the BRP desk of an international trader such as Axpo, TotalEnergies or Vattenfall, a gas shipper such as EBN, the in-house BRP of a Dutch supplier, or Eneve's own BRP as a Service desk that carries balance responsibility for suppliers with portfolios from 40 GWh. Works in 15-minute programme time units with a 24-hour operations rota and a gate closure that never moves.
careAbout: A day-ahead forecast per EAN type, including solar, wind, batteries and telemetry connections, that is good enough that the E-programme is right before the intraday desk has to fix it
Every nomination and re-nomination to TenneT and the gas TSO submitted before gate closure, with a confirmed receipt and an alert when an interface fails, day and night
An intraday position per 15-minute block that is near real time, so the desk decides to trade on ETPA or steer assets while it still matters
Allocation and reconciliation volumes from the TenneT MMC-Hub that match nominations and meter data, with rejections and deviations handled the same day rather than in the next reconciliation run
An imbalance settlement invoice from TenneT that can be verified line by line against the portfolio's own data and passed on to the right segment or customer
Imbalance cost per MWh that falls year on year and can be shown to management and to the suppliers the desk serves
winsThem: Forecasting, nomination and re-nomination for electricity and gas as one automated cycle with the operator supervising exceptions, instead of scripts and spreadsheets stitched together by whoever is on shift
An ETPA intraday trading cycle run as a guaranteed process with position, price and volume limits, so the desk closes the gap in the position without a trader watching a screen all night
Steering signals to batteries, solar parks and flexible customer assets from the same position the trades are made on, with the effect visible in the next 15-minute block

Allocation 2.0 reconciliation, MMC-Hub exchange and imbalance settlement verification handled in the same data model as the nominations, so a dispute is an exception report rather than a research project
The option to outsource the whole cycle as BRP as a Service with tiered per-MWh pricing, keeping the portfolio visibility while the operational risk moves to a specialist desk
theirFear: A missed gate closure on a windy Sunday because the nomination interface failed silently and nobody on shift saw it, leaving a full day of imbalance at prices that wipe out a month of margin
A reconciliation run that reveals the portfolio was allocated volumes it never nominated because a switch batch had not reached the BRP's register, months after the fact
A steering signal that discharges a customer's battery at the wrong moment and turns a hedge into an imbalance position while the customer's site loses power quality

jobsToBeDone.name: Forecast and nominate the portfolio accurately and on time
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Every day, for every EAN type in the portfolio, produce the day-ahead forecast, match it to the procured position, build and submit the E-programme to TenneT and the gas nominations to the gas TSO before gate closure, update the forecast intraday and re-nominate when the position changes, and review ex post how good the forecast was.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Nominations reflect the best available forecast and the procured volumes, arrive before every gate closure with a confirmed receipt, and are corrected intraday as the position changes, so the imbalance the desk has to settle is the residual that could not be known, not the result of a missed deadline or a stale forecast.

steps.step: Assemble the portfolio master data and EAN register
steps.description: Keep the list of connections the BRP is responsible for current: EANs per supplier and connection type (small consumers, telemetry, producers, batteries, BSP and flex assets), switches in and out, and the mapping to the segments and grid areas the forecast and the allocation use.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Receives the BRP-related market messages and register updates from EDSN, C-AR and TenneT that keep the EAN portfolio current.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Maintains the portfolio register per BRP, supplier and EAN type that allocation and nominations are grouped by.

steps.step: Produce the day-ahead forecast per EAN type
steps.description: Run the day-ahead forecast per 15-minute block from consumption profiles, telemetry history, weather and solar and wind production forecasts, including the batteries and flexible assets whose planned schedules the desk knows, and review the segments with the largest expected error.

streamsNeeded.name: Forecast and Nominate the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs the day-ahead forecast models per EAN type and presents the forecast and its expected error for review.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect and Validate Meter Data
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides validated telemetry and consumption history that the forecast models are trained and corrected on.

steps.step: Match the forecast to the procured position and build the E-programme
steps.description: Compare the forecast with the volumes procured on the forward and 15-minute day-ahead markets, decide how to close the difference, and compile the E-programme and gas nominations per grid area and counterparty.

streamsNeeded.name: Forecast and Nominate the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Builds the position per 15-minute block and compiles the E-programme and gas nominations from forecast and trades.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Supplies the executed hedges and day-ahead purchases that the forecast is matched against.

steps.step: Submit nominations to TenneT and the gas TSO before gate closure
steps.description: Send the E-programme to TenneT and the hourly gas nominations to the gas TSO through the certified interfaces, confirm the acknowledgements, and handle rejections before the deadline, with an alert to the shift operator when an interface or acknowledgement is missing.

streamsNeeded.name: Forecast and Nominate the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Submits the nominations, tracks acknowledgements and rejections and escalates when a deadline is at risk.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Operates the TenneT and gas TSO nomination interfaces and monitors their availability.

steps.step: Update the forecast intraday and re-nominate
steps.description: Refresh the forecast as telemetry, weather updates and intraday trades come in, and submit re-nominations up to the intraday gate closure whenever the position has moved enough to matter.

streamsNeeded.name: Forecast and Nominate the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs the intraday forecast update and generates re-nominations from the changed position.

streamsNeeded.name: Steer Intraday and Optimise Imbalance
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Feeds the intraday trades and steering actions back into the position that is re-nominated.

steps.step: Review forecast quality ex post
steps.description: Compare nominated, forecast and allocated volumes per EAN type and 15-minute block after allocation arrives, attribute the error to weather, profiles, switches or assets, and tune the models and the review rules.

streamsNeeded.name: Forecast and Nominate the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs the ex-post forecast evaluation and stores the error attribution used to retune the models.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the allocated volumes that the ex-post evaluation compares the forecast and nominations with.

jobsToBeDone.name: Steer intraday to minimise imbalance cost
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Within the day, watch the portfolio position per 15-minute block against the E-programme, decide whether to close deviations by trading on ETPA or by steering batteries, solar parks and flexible customer assets, execute those actions as a guaranteed cycle, and learn from the imbalance result of every block.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Deviations from the programme are closed at the cheapest available action before the block is settled, steering never harms a customer's site, and the imbalance cost per MWh falls towards the portfolio's residual, unavoidable level.

steps.step: Watch the near real-time position per 15-minute block
steps.description: Follow the position of the portfolio per block from telemetry, estimated small-consumer volumes and asset schedules, compared with the nominated programme and with the expected imbalance price direction published by TenneT.

streamsNeeded.name: Steer Intraday and Optimise Imbalance
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Maintains the near real-time intraday position and the deviation from the programme per block.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect and Validate Meter Data
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Streams telemetry from large and flexible connections into the intraday position.

steps.step: Decide between trading and steering
steps.description: For each material deviation, compare the cost of an ETPA trade with the cost and feasibility of steering an asset, taking the imbalance price expectation, asset constraints and customer agreements into account, and choose the action or deliberately keep the position.

streamsNeeded.name: Steer Intraday and Optimise Imbalance
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Presents the action options per deviation with their expected cost and the constraints of the available assets.

steps.step: Run the ETPA intraday trading cycle
steps.description: Place and manage intraday orders on ETPA within volume and price limits as a guaranteed cycle that runs around the clock, confirm fills and apply them to the position and the re-nomination.

streamsNeeded.name: Steer Intraday and Optimise Imbalance
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs the intraday trading cycle with limits, order management and fill confirmation.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Operates the ETPA trading interface and monitors its availability and latency.

steps.step: Dispatch steering signals to flexible assets
steps.description: Send charge, discharge, curtail or shift signals to batteries, solar parks, CHP units and curtailable industrial load within the constraints agreed with the asset owners, and confirm the response in telemetry.

streamsNeeded.name: Steer Intraday and Optimise Imbalance
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Generates and dispatches steering signals and tracks the asset response per block.

streamsNeeded.name: Trade and Manage Customer Energy Contracts
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Holds the flexibility agreements and asset constraints of customers whose assets may be steered.

steps.step: Evaluate the imbalance result per block and tune
steps.description: After settlement data arrives, review the imbalance volume and cost per block, which actions paid off and which did not, and adjust limits, thresholds and steering rules.

streamsNeeded.name: Steer Intraday and Optimise Imbalance
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Reports the imbalance result per block against the actions taken and lets the operator tune the rules.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the settled imbalance volumes and prices per block that the evaluation is based on.

jobsToBeDone.name: Settle allocation, reconciliation and imbalance without disputes
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: After delivery, receive the allocation and reconciliation volumes for the portfolio through the TenneT MMC-Hub under Allocation 2.0, check them against nominations and meter data, process the reconciliation runs, verify the imbalance settlement invoice from TenneT, and report BRP compliance while passing the costs to the segments and customers they belong to.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Allocated, reconciled and settled volumes agree with the portfolio's own data, the imbalance invoice is verified before it is paid, costs are attributed to the right segment or customer, and no settlement dispute or compliance finding surprises the desk months later.

steps.step: Receive and validate allocation messages from the MMC-Hub
steps.description: Ingest the allocation volumes per EAN type and grid area from the TenneT market-to-market communication hub, validate them for completeness and format, and handle rejected or missing messages with the sending party the same day.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Processes the allocation messages, validates them and raises exceptions for rejections and gaps.

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Operates the MMC-Hub connection and monitors message flow and acknowledgements.

steps.step: Compare allocated, nominated and metered volumes
steps.description: Reconcile allocated volumes with the E-programme and with validated meter data per block and EAN type, and investigate the deviations that exceed thresholds, such as switches that had not reached the BRP register or telemetry gaps estimated by the grid operator.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs the three-way comparison and lists the deviations per block with their probable cause.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect and Validate Meter Data
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the validated metered volumes the allocation is compared against.

steps.step: Process the Allocation 2.0 reconciliation runs
steps.description: Handle the periodic reconciliation for small-consumer and telemetry connections introduced with Allocation 2.0 tranche 3 on 1 January 2025, apply the corrected volumes and their financial effect to the portfolio, and record what changed against the original allocation.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Applies the reconciliation volumes and prices, keeps the audit trail against the original allocation and reports the financial effect.

steps.step: Verify the imbalance settlement invoice
steps.description: Recalculate the imbalance volume and cost per block from the portfolio's own allocation and programme data and the published imbalance prices, compare with TenneT's settlement, and raise a dispute where the difference exceeds the tolerance.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Recomputes the imbalance settlement per block and flags the lines that differ from the TSO invoice.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the traded volumes and prices that determine the programme against which imbalance is calculated.

steps.step: Report compliance and pass costs to segments and customers
steps.description: Produce the BRP compliance reporting for TenneT and the regulator, attribute imbalance and reconciliation costs to segments, suppliers served and individual large customers, and hand the volumes and costs to billing where they are invoiced.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Generates the compliance reports and the cost attribution per segment and customer.

streamsNeeded.name: Bill and Reconcile Customers
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Invoices the attributed imbalance and reconciliation costs to the suppliers and large customers that carry them.

customerJourneyStories.name: A supplier outsources balance responsibility to BRP as a Service
customerJourneyStories.summary: The balancing operator of a growing renewable supplier, whose in-house BRP setup could not keep up with Allocation 2.0 reconciliation, the 15-minute day-ahead market and rising imbalance prices, moves the portfolio to BRP as a Service and keeps the visibility while the operational risk moves to a specialist desk.

stages.narrative: In the first quarter of 2025 the reconciliation runs under Allocation 2.0 tranche 3 produce corrections the supplier's two-person BRP team cannot explain, imbalance costs on windy weekends have doubled with the portfolio's solar and wind share, and the 15-minute day-ahead change in September is approaching with a forecasting script that only knows hours. The director asks whether the company should still carry balance responsibility itself.

The operator finds Eneve's BRP as a Service page and the March 2025 announcement of the collaboration with Pure Energie, hears the managed-BRP proposition described at a TenneT market-party day, and asks the supplier's billing colleagues, who already run on the platform, for an introduction. A call with the operations desk explains the guaranteed forecasting, nomination and ETPA cycle and the claim of up to 53% lower imbalance cost.

The supplier compares hiring two more operators and rebuilding the tooling, joining another BRP's portfolio, and BRP as a Service. Decisive checks are the 40 GWh minimum portfolio and the tiered per-MWh pricing against the current imbalance and staff cost, how the supplier keeps its own position and cost visibility per segment, who is liable for a missed nomination, whether batteries and BSP assets are covered, and a reference call with a comparable supplier.

For one month the service runs in shadow mode: the desk forecasts and builds nominations for the supplier's portfolio next to the in-house team, and both results are compared with allocation per block. The shadow forecast is better for every EAN type, and a re-nomination the in-house team missed on a holiday would have cost more than a month of service fees.

Balance responsibility is transferred at the start of a month. The operator's role shifts to supervising the daily reports, the 15-minute financial insight per segment and the reconciliation results, and to feeding the desk with campaign volumes and new producer connections. The intraday cycle runs at night without anyone at the supplier awake.

After the first year the imbalance cost per MWh has fallen well below the in-house level, the supplier adds its first battery customers to the steered portfolio, and the operator becomes the reference other suppliers call. Taking the role back would mean rebuilding a 24-hour desk and the tooling the service made unnecessary.

customerJourneyStories.name: A gas shipper adopts the Balancing and Shipping Suite for nominations and trading
customerJourneyStories.summary: The shipping operator of a gas producer and shipper, whose nomination and position management ran on a legacy in-house tool, adopts the Balancing and Shipping Suite for gas trading and shipping and ends up with automated nominations, verified settlements and a desk that can add electricity later.

stages.narrative: The shipper's in-house nomination tool, maintained by one retiring developer, fails a gas TSO interface change and a day of nominations has to be entered by hand. The board wants shipping and trading operations on a supported platform before the next gas year.

The operator knows the EBASE name from years of BRP market messages and finds that Energy21 has become Eneve, that EBN signed a gas trading and shipping agreement with it on 10 September 2024, and that the Balancing and Shipping Suite covers automated nominations and position management for both gas and electricity. A visit to the operations desk in Utrecht shows the nomination cycle and the settlement verification live.

The shipper evaluates the suite against a European gas trading system and a rebuild of the in-house tool. The checks that matter are the certified gas TSO interfaces and their monitoring, the handling of hourly nominations and re-nominations, how the suite verifies allocation and settlement against the shipper's own measurements, the security and continuity documentation for the auditors, and the option to add electricity balance responsibility later on the same platform.

A three-month pilot runs the nominations for one portion of the portfolio through the suite in parallel with the legacy tool, with the legacy tool remaining the system of record. The pilot delivers every nomination before gate closure, catches two settlement lines the shipper would have paid without question, and proves the interface monitoring during a planned TSO maintenance window.

The full portfolio moves at the start of the gas year. Nominations, position management and settlement verification run as one cycle, the operator works from exception lists instead of screens, and the trading desk sees the shipped position next to its trades. The legacy tool is switched off after two clean months.

At renewal the shipper extends the contract to include electricity nominations for its power assets and asks the desk for regulatory reporting from the same data. The suite is now the system the auditors and the TSO relationship depend on.

customers.name: Industrial Energy Manager
customers.description: Manages energy procurement and consumption for an industrial company with several large connections: a chemical or process site such as BASF's Dutch operations or the USG utility company at the Chemelot site, a food or metals producer with multiple plants, or a wind and solar producer selling its output. Holds a multi-site framework supply contract with a supplier, executes click trades within it, submits consumption forecasts, analyses consumption per site and process, and runs flexible assets such as batteries, CHP units and curtailable load whose value depends on the market. Works through the customer trading self-service of the supplier's platform, judged on the energy cost per unit of production and on never causing an unplanned outage.
careAbout: Consumption and production per site, connection and process visible per 15-minute block from validated meter data, not from the supplier's invoice weeks later
A forecast per site that reflects the production plan, so the supplier and BRP nominate the right volume and the site does not pay for deviations it could have announced
Clicking tranches of the framework contract when the price is right, within limits agreed with the supplier, without a phone call and with immediate confirmation
Contract changes such as an added site, a changed volume band or a new connection processed in days and reflected on the next invoice
Flexibility from batteries, CHP and curtailable load monetised through the supplier's BRP without any risk to production or power quality
An invoice per site that matches the clicked prices, the measured volumes and the flex revenue, so the plant controller signs it without a query
winsThem: A customer trading desk in the supplier's portal where the framework contract, the click windows, the executed clicks and the open volume are one screen, with price alerts that reach the manager on the plant floor
Consumption analysis and forecast management per site fed by the same validated meter data the supplier bills on, with the production plan as an input
Steering of batteries, CHP and curtailable load by the BRP within constraints the site sets, with the activations and revenue visible per block and settled on the invoice
Multi-site invoices with a breakdown per connection, click and cost component that the site controllers can reconcile against their own measurements
A supplier that can price, contract and connect a new site in days because the deal, the contract and the switch run on one platform
theirFear: A click executed at a mistyped volume or in the wrong delivery period that binds the company to a year of energy at the wrong price, with nobody at the supplier catching it
A steering signal that curtails a process or drains a battery when production needs it, so a few thousand euros of flex revenue cost a day of output
A multi-site invoice that mixes up connections or ignores the clicked prices, discovered by the plant controller after it has been paid and booked

jobsToBeDone.name: Understand and forecast energy consumption per site
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Connect every site's meters and telemetry, analyse consumption and production per site, connection and process, build a forecast driven by the production plan, share it with the supplier and BRP so the portfolio is nominated correctly, and reconcile the invoiced volumes with the site's own measurements.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: The energy manager knows where every MWh goes per site and block, the forecast the supplier nominates on reflects the plant's real plan, deviations are announced instead of settled, and every invoiced volume can be traced to a measurement.

steps.step: Connect all sites' meters and telemetry
steps.description: Register every connection and sub-meter of the sites in the supplier's platform, connect telemetry and smart-meter data, and check that each connection's data arrives validated per 15-minute block.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect and Validate Meter Data

streamsNeeded.name: Integrate Market Communication and External Systems
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Connects meter-data providers and site telemetry systems to the platform.

steps.step: Analyse consumption per site, process and shift
steps.description: Break consumption and production down per site, connection, production line and shift, compare with the production output, and find the loads that drive peaks, off-spec consumption and avoidable cost.

streamsNeeded.name: Trade and Manage Customer Energy Contracts
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the consumption analysis self-service per site and process on top of validated meter data.

streamsNeeded.name: Collect and Validate Meter Data
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Supplies the interval history and clustered data the analysis is built on.

steps.step: Build a production-plan-driven forecast
steps.description: Combine the production schedule, maintenance stops, weather-dependent loads and the historical profile into a consumption forecast per site and block for the coming days, weeks and months.

streamsNeeded.name: Trade and Manage Customer Energy Contracts
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Offers forecast management in which the site enters production plans and stops and reviews the resulting forecast.

streamsNeeded.name: Forecast and Nominate the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Turns the site forecast into the portfolio forecast the supplier's BRP nominates on.

steps.step: Share the forecast and track deviations
steps.description: Submit the forecast to the supplier before its nomination deadline, update it when production changes, and see the deviation between forecast and measured consumption per block together with the cost it caused.

streamsNeeded.name: Trade and Manage Customer Energy Contracts
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Handles forecast submission, updates and the deviation view per site.

streamsNeeded.name: Forecast and Nominate the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Applies the updated site forecast to the intraday forecast and re-nomination of the portfolio.

steps.step: Reconcile invoiced volumes with own measurements
steps.description: Compare the volumes on the multi-site invoice with the site's own measurements and the validated meter data, and raise a query where a connection, period or component differs.

streamsNeeded.name: Settle, Allocate and Reconcile Market Volumes
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the allocated and reconciled volumes per connection that explain differences between invoice and measurement.

jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Within a multi-site framework contract, follow the market, execute click trades for tranches and delivery periods when the price fits the company's procurement policy, change the contract when a site is added or volumes shift, and check that every invoice reflects the clicked prices.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: The company buys its energy at prices it chose, within limits agreed with the supplier, with each click confirmed in minutes and reflected in the position and the invoice, and contract changes done in days instead of weeks of email.

streamsNeeded.name: Trade and Manage Customer Energy Contracts
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Presents the framework contract, click rules and open volume per period on the customer trading desk.

steps.step: Watch price curves and set alerts
steps.description: Follow the forward curves and the day-ahead prices for the delivery periods still open, define the target prices from the company's procurement policy, and receive alerts when a curve reaches them.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Provides the maintained price curves the click prices are derived from.

streamsNeeded.name: Trade and Manage Customer Energy Contracts
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Offers price alerts and indicative click prices per delivery period on the trading desk.

streamsNeeded.name: Trade and Manage Customer Energy Contracts
streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Executes the click within the limits, confirms it and records it against the contract and the supplier's position.

streamsNeeded.name: Source and Price the Portfolio

streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Captures the contract change request and routes it through pricing and approval.

streamsNeeded.howItSupports: Runs the switch or move-in of the added connection through market communication.

jobsToBeDone.name: Monetise flexible assets without operational risk
jobsToBeDone.whatItIs: Take stock of the site's flexible assets and their constraints, agree with the supplier and its BRP how they may be steered and paid for, connect them to the steering signals with safeguards, run and monitor activations, and verify that the flex revenue on the invoice matches the activations.
jobsToBeDone.outcome: Batteries, CHP units and curtailable load earn imbalance, intraday and reserve revenue within limits the site controls, activations never harm production, and the revenue is settled transparently on the same invoice as the supply.

customerJourneyStories.name: Taking multi-site procurement onto the supplier's customer trading desk
customerJourneyStories.summary: The energy manager of a chemical group with several Dutch sites adopts the customer trading and forecast self-service offered through the supplier's platform after a year of phone-executed clicks and disputed invoices, and ends up running procurement for all sites from one desk.

stages.narrative: A click for a full calendar year is executed by phone at a price that differs from the confirmation email, the multi-site invoice for the quarter mixes up two connections, and the group's CFO asks why energy, the second-largest cost, is bought on the phone and checked on paper. The energy manager wants the same control over energy as over any other commodity.

The supplier's key account manager mentions that its platform now includes a customer trading desk with click contracts and forecast management, and sends the case description of an industrial customer. At an industrial energy users' association meeting the energy manager hears a peer from a site utility company describe clicking tranches from a tablet.

The energy manager and the procurement director compare staying with phone clicks, engaging a broker, and using the supplier's trading desk. They check the click limits and four-eyes approval, whether the framework contract terms are represented correctly, how the site's own measurements can be reconciled with the invoice breakdown, the audit trail for the internal auditors, and whether a second supplier's platform would lock them in.

For one quarter one site runs on the trading desk while the others stay on the phone. The manager executes three clicks with confirmation in minutes, submits the site's forecast from the production plan, and reconciles the quarterly invoice per connection without a query for the first time.

All sites move to the desk at the framework renewal. Price alerts arrive on the plant floor, the site controllers get their own read-only access to consumption and invoices, and the forecast per site is updated whenever a maintenance stop is planned. The CFO receives a monthly view of clicked prices against the market.

The group renews the framework contract with the supplier for another three years, partly because the trading desk has become the group's procurement tool, and asks the supplier about steering its new battery. Moving to another supplier would mean losing the click history, forecasts and reconciled invoices per site.

customerJourneyStories.name: Monetising a site battery and CHP through the supplier's BRP
customerJourneyStories.summary: The utility manager of an industrial site with a new battery and an existing CHP unit adopts the flexible-asset steering offered through the supplier's platform and BRP, after being courted by aggregators, and ends up with flex revenue on the same invoice as supply and constraints the site controls.

stages.narrative: The site's new 10 MW battery sits mostly idle after commissioning, the CHP unit is run on a fixed schedule regardless of the market, and three aggregators have offered to take over the assets with contracts the site's engineers do not trust. The board wants the assets to earn money without a single production incident.

The supplier, whose BRP already nominates the site, explains that its balancing platform steers batteries, CHP and curtailable load within customer constraints and that the value is settled on the supply invoice. The utility manager reads about the November 2025 aFRR changes with 0.1 MW setpoints and 4-hour capacity auctions and asks how the site's assets could qualify.

The site compares the aggregator offers with steering through the supplier's BRP. The engineers test the constraint model, the override and the emergency stop; the controller compares the revenue share and the settlement transparency; the energy manager checks the imbalance, intraday and aFRR use cases and whether the site keeps its own view of every activation. A reference call with another steered industrial site settles the engineers' doubts.

A three-month pilot steers the battery only, within conservative state-of-charge limits and outside production-critical hours. Every activation is visible per block, the constraints hold during a test override, and the pilot revenue appears on the next invoice with a breakdown per activation.

The CHP unit and a curtailable process are added to the agreement, the constraints are widened after the engineers see the response data, and the site's utility team checks the activation report every morning. The aFRR product is added when the assets are prequalified.

The site renews the flexibility agreement together with the supply contract, adds a second battery sized on the activation data, and the utility manager presents the setup to the group's other sites. The aggregators stop calling once the site's flex revenue and its supply are settled on one invoice.

top.name: Energy cost per unit of production
top.description: Net energy cost of the sites, including supply, imbalance and pass-through costs minus flexibility revenue, per tonne of product. Modeled seed value for an energy-intensive Dutch industrial group, not an official customer figure.

branches.name: Forecast and procurement quality
branches.description: How accurately the sites forecast their consumption and how well the framework contract's clicks are executed against the market.

children.name: Forecast deviation rate
children.description: Mean absolute deviation between the submitted site forecast and the measured consumption per 15-minute block, as a share of the forecast, over the month.

children.name: Site forecasts submitted on time
children.description: Share of days on which every site's forecast reached the supplier before its nomination deadline.

children.name: Production plan changes reflected within a day
children.description: Share of production plan changes and maintenance stops reflected in the submitted forecast within one working day.

children.name: Clicked price versus market average
children.description: Volume-weighted average clicked price for a delivery year compared with the average forward price of that year over the click window, negative when the sites bought below average.

children.name: Framework volume clicked before the delivery month
children.description: Share of the framework contract volume clicked before the start of the delivery month rather than left to the default price.

children.name: Click execution turnaround
children.description: Minutes between the manager's click request and the binding confirmation with the executed price.

branches.name: Flexibility value and invoice trust
branches.description: How much the flexible assets earn without harming production, and whether the invoices per site can be trusted without a query.

children.name: Flexibility revenue captured
children.description: Annual revenue from imbalance steering, intraday optimisation and reserve products earned by the sites' batteries, CHP units and curtailable load.

children.name: Flex activation success rate
children.description: Share of steering activations delivered within the agreed constraints without a production impact or an override.

children.name: Asset availability for steering
children.description: Share of hours in which the flexible assets were available to the BRP for steering within their constraints.

children.name: Invoice deviation from own measurement
children.description: Absolute difference between invoiced volumes and the sites' own validated measurements as a share of invoiced volume.

children.name: Multi-site invoices reconciled without query
children.description: Share of multi-site invoices the site controllers approved without raising a query or dispute.

children.name: Contract changes processed within agreed time
children.description: Share of site additions, volume band changes and extensions completed within the time agreed in the framework contract.

top.name: Industrial volume traded through the platform
top.description: Annual volume of large consumers and producers whose click trades, forecasts and flexibility are managed through the customer trading capabilities of suppliers on the platform. Modeled seed value for the large-customer segment, not an official Eneve figure.

branches.name: Large-customer self-service adoption
branches.description: How many industrial customers use the trading desk through their supplier and how much of their trading happens digitally without desk intervention.

children.name: Industrial customers active on the trading desk
children.description: Number of large consumers and producers with an active customer trading account across all supplier tenants.

children.name: Suppliers offering the customer trading desk
children.description: Number of supplier tenants that have enabled the customer trading desk for their business customers.

children.name: Monthly active industrial users
children.description: Share of industrial customer accounts that logged in and used analysis, forecasting or trading in the month.

children.name: Click trades executed digitally
children.description: Share of click trades of industrial customers executed through the trading desk rather than by phone or email to the supplier's desk.

children.name: Click trades per customer per year
children.description: Average number of click trades executed per active industrial customer per year.

children.name: Trades requiring desk intervention
children.description: Share of digital click trades that needed manual handling by the supplier's desk because of limit breaches, pricing gaps or errors.

branches.name: Flexibility and services value
branches.description: How much flexible capacity is connected through the platform and what the large-customer segment earns for the suppliers and the platform.

children.name: Flexible capacity connected
children.description: Total steerable capacity of industrial batteries, CHP units and curtailable loads connected to steering through the platform.

children.name: Battery and CHP assets steered
children.description: Number of industrial batteries and CHP units under active steering agreements.

children.name: aFRR-capable capacity share
children.description: Share of the connected flexible capacity prequalified for aFRR participation under the 0.1 MW setpoint regime.

children.name: Customer trading revenue
children.description: Annual recurring revenue from customer trading, consumption self-service and flexibility modules attributable to the large-customer segment.

children.name: Revenue per industrial customer
children.description: Annual customer trading and flexibility module revenue divided by the number of active industrial customers.

children.name: Industrial customer churn rate
children.description: Share of industrial customers per year that stop using the trading desk, including those that switch to a supplier not on the platform.
